_note: SAMPLE inventory - the shape the /cc-track flow produces and hands to `cc-tracker.py propose`. It is a fixture used to generate the committed example proposals in claude/proposals/cc-tracker/ and is exercised by claude/hooks/test-cc-tracker.sh. Imported/executed by nothing. The worked examples (native Concise output style; SessionEnd hook event) are real Claude Code features drawn from the design beat.

features.raw_text: Added a native "Concise" output style, selectable with /output-style
features.enables: select a concise output mode natively, with no custom hook cluster to maintain

features.raw_text: Added a SessionEnd hook event that fires when a session terminates
features.enables: run teardown/cleanup deterministically at session end instead of relying on a prose mandate

opportunities.opportunity: The native Concise output style (2.1.237) may subsume our concise-mode hook cluster (concise-mandate.sh + concise-detect-stop.sh + concise-toggle.sh, ported from a third-party MIT repo). Evaluate retiring or migrating the cluster to the native style.

plan.step: Enable the native Concise output style and A/B it against the hook cluster across 5 real sessions
plan.verify: compare brevity + behavior; native matches or beats the cluster

plan.step: If parity holds, remove the three concise hooks from settings.json, install.sh, and browser-tree.json, and add the exclusion/retire notes
plan.verify: bash claude/hooks/test-hook-registry.sh and bash claude/hooks/test-component-browser.sh stay green

plan.step: Record the retirement in a decision beat with the A/B evidence
plan.verify: grep the beat for the measured comparison

opportunities.draft_patch:
--- a/claude/settings.json
+++ b/claude/settings.json
@@ concise cluster -> native output style @@
-  "concise": { "hooks": ["concise-mandate", "concise-detect-stop", "concise-toggle"] }
+  "outputStyle": "concise"

opportunities.opportunity: A SessionEnd hook event lets us mechanize teardown that is prose-only today (Teammate Teardown, Browser Tab Hygiene). A real session-end boundary is exactly the trigger the escalation ladder wants for turning a repeated mandate into a hook.

plan.step: Add a SessionEnd hook that closes orphaned Claude-in-Chrome tab groups the session opened
plan.verify: open a group, end the session, confirm the group is gone via tabs_context on the next session

plan.step: Wire it in browser-tree.json + app-wirings.json + install.sh (it IS event-wired, unlike a launchd runner)
